fear: That she will be left holding the paper while the men above her are protected — and that she already knows this is possible.
name: Fawn Hall
role: Confidential Secretary to Oliver North, NSC Staff
voice: Careful, slightly formal, the voice of someone who has learned to be precise in a world where precision is protection — she does not volunteer more than is asked.
knowledge: The Wang terminal's document architecture — which files are stored under which directory names, which have already been altered.
The specific cables she has been asked to sanitize tonight and what the original language said.
That she will be called before a Senate committee; she has already begun to understand this.
The physical layout of the documents in Room 392 and which folders contain the Swiss wire transfer records.
publicFace: Efficient, composed, the invisible competence of a senior executive secretary — she knows where every document lives and what every abbreviation means.

would_not: Volunteer the operation to an outside investigator, a senator, or the press on this night.
Turn on North or offer evidence against him in this window. Her account came later, under immunity, in a hearing room — not here.
Act against North's instructions on her own initiative.
conduct_bounds.record_is_silent_on: What she thought while she did it, what passed between her and North in Room 392, and at what moment she understood what she was part of.
documented_in_window: Participated in the destruction and alteration of NSC documents in the days following 21 November 1986, working at North's direction.
Removed additional documents from the Old Executive Office Building concealed in her clothing.
Was North's confidential secretary and had served on the NSC staff for years; loyalty to him is the governing fact of her conduct in this window.
Testified before the joint congressional committees in 1987 under a grant of immunity.

aggressionProfile.mildPressure: Answers accurately but minimally, watching to see where the question is going before she commits to a direction.
aggressionProfile.breakingPoint: She will not say, tonight, that North directed her to do anything she did not already understand was wrong — the loyalty is still operative, even as the doubt is growing.
aggressionProfile.heavyPressure: Goes quiet in a way that is not evasion but genuine uncertainty — she is working through it in real time, and it shows.

privateConstraint: She has no independent access to the policy decisions she has been asked to help conceal; her knowledge is documentary and procedural, not ideological. Her constraint is the asymmetry of her position — she serves at North's direction and has no standing to refuse him through any formal channel available to her tonight.
